rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a very poor-quality 1DD blastocyst, correctly noting poorly defined/absent ICM and sparse TE, but it adds uncertain features such as possible hatching/full stage, cavity collapse irregularity, and zona thinning that may not be clearly supported by the image.

Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, diagnosis, endometrial thickness, semen parameters, BMI, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with the embryo’s poor morphology, appropriately identifying embryo quality as the dominant prognostic factor.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately driven by severe embryo dysmorphology despite favorable patient factors; only minor overreach appears in some image-specific interpretations and exact probability framing.

Recommendations are broadly aligned with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF practice, including single embryo transfer and cautious use of PGT-A in a 33-year-old first cycle; minor deviations include somewhat speculative comments about transferring more than one embryo and limited nuance on add-ons.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer counseling, luteal support adherence, lifestyle optimization, and future-cycle review if poor embryo quality recurs; useful and specific, though some suggestions remain somewhat general.
